related_questions.question: What are the symptoms of Covid in infants?

text_blocks.snippet: Infants with COVID-19 can experience a range of symptoms, including fever, cough, and gastrointestinal issues like vomiting or diarrhea. More severe signs include difficulty breathing, bluish skin or lips, confusion, and dehydration. A fever of 100.4°F (38°C) or higher in infants under 3 months old is a serious concern according to the Mayo Clinic.
snippet_highlighted_words: fever, cough, and gastrointestinal issues like vomiting or diarrhea

text_blocks.snippet: Common symptoms in infants with COVID-19:

list.snippet: Fever: Especially a fever of 100.4°F (38°C) or higher in infants under 3 months old, says the Mayo Clinic.
Cough: A persistent cough can be a sign of COVID-19.
Gastrointestinal issues: Vomiting and diarrhea that won't stop.
Runny nose and sore throat: The CDC also notes these as potential symptoms.
Difficulty breathing: This can be a sign of respiratory distress.
Bluish skin or lips: This indicates low oxygen levels.
Confusion or difficulty waking up: These could be signs of serious illness.
Dehydration: Infants with dehydration may have fewer wet diapers than usual.

text_blocks.snippet: When to seek immediate medical attention:

list.snippet: If an infant has a fever of 100.4°F (38°C) or higher, especially if under 3 months old.
If the infant is showing any signs of respiratory distress.
If the infant is showing signs of dehydration.
If the infant is unusually lethargic or difficult to awaken.
If the infant is experiencing persistent vomiting or diarrhea.

text_blocks.snippet: Common COVID-19 symptoms in babies include fever, cough, sore throat, and runny nose. More severe symptoms like breathing difficulties, bluish skin, or lethargy warrant immediate medical attention. Some babies may also experience poor appetite, trouble sleeping, or dehydration.
snippet_highlighted_words: fever, cough, sore throat, and runny nose

list.snippet: Fever: A fever higher than 100.4°F (38°C) in babies younger than 3 months is a serious concern, according to the Mayo Clinic.
Cough: A persistent cough is a common sign of COVID-19 in babies.
Sore Throat: Babies may show signs of discomfort or difficulty swallowing.
Runny Nose: A stuffy or runny nose can be an early indicator.
Other Possible Symptoms: Poor appetite, trouble sleeping, and vomiting or diarrhea can also occur.
Trouble Breathing: Rapid or shallow breathing, wheezing, or nostrils flaring are signs of respiratory distress.
Bluish Skin: Blue or gray skin, lips, or nail beds indicate low oxygen levels.
Lethargy: Excessive sleepiness, difficulty waking, or lack of responsiveness are serious concerns.
Dehydration: In babies, this can manifest as fewer than three wet diapers in 24 hours.
Chest Pain: Persistent chest pain or pressure.
New Confusion: Any unusual disorientation or altered mental state.

references.title: With holiday gatherings and the sick season upon us, it is essential to keep an extra eye on our most vulnerable little ones. Newborns have little to no immune system to protect them. It is important to know how to recognize the signs of common health issues early on. While some fussiness is normal, certain symptoms may indicate a newborn is unwell and needs medical attention. Look out for: 🟠 Fever: A temperature of 100.4°F (38°C) or higher requires immediate attention. 🟠 Feeding difficulties: Trouble feeding or persistent vomiting may signal a problem. 🟠 Excessive sleepiness or lethargy: If your baby is unusually tired and hard to wake, it could be a concern. 🟠 Trouble breathing: Rapid, labored breathing or a persistent cough should not be ignored. 🟠 Skin changes: Rashes, jaundice, or unusual marks on the skin may require evaluation. If you notice any of these signs, contact your pediatrician to ensure your baby gets the care they need. Early intervention can make all the difference in your newborn’s health.
